audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is block RLP size validated before any processing occurs (EIP-7934)?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. EIP-7934 MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE validation is an Execution Layer concern. Prysm is a Consensus Layer client and does not perform RLP block size validation. The CL receives execution payloads via Engine API, not raw RLP-encoded blocks from P2P.

code_scope.resolution: No corresponding code in Prysm CL client

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are blocks with non-empty ommers rejected in post-merge Ethereum?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Ommer/uncle validation is an Execution Layer block validation concern. Prysm as a CL client does not process or validate EL block ommers. Post-merge, ommers are an EL header field validated by execution clients (Geth, Besu, etc.).

code_scope.resolution: No corresponding code in Prysm CL client

The 8 computed roots/hashes (gas_used, transactions_root, state_root, receipt_root, bloom, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, requests_hash) are computed and validated by the Execution Layer during state_transition. Prysm CL delegates block execution to the EL via Engine API and trusts the EL's validation.

audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. ECDSA transaction sender recovery (ecrecover) is an Execution Layer operation. Prysm uses BLS signatures for CL operations, not ECDSA for EL transactions. Transaction sender identity derivation is performed by EL clients.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding deterministic and collision-free?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. RLP encoding/decoding is an Execution Layer serialization format. Prysm CL uses SSZ (Simple Serialize) for its serialization needs. While Prysm has minor RLP dependencies for interop, it does not implement core RLP encoding logic for block structures.

code_scope.resolution: No corresponding code in Prysm CL client

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 collision-resistant and correctly implemented?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. While Prysm does use keccak256 for certain operations, the property specifically concerns EL block hash computation and state root verification (trust boundaries tb-002, tb-005). Prysm's keccak256 usage is for CL-side operations and relies on well-audited Go standard library implementations (golang.org/x/crypto/sha3).

code_scope.resolution: Property targets EL block hash computation, not CL usage

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is withdrawal amount scaled correctly by 10^9 (Gwei to Wei)?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The Gwei-to-Wei scaling (10^9 multiplication) in process_withdrawals is an Execution Layer operation. Prysm CL handles withdrawals at the CL level (selecting validators for withdrawal, constructing withdrawal lists) but the balance credit in Wei is performed by the EL. The trust boundaries tb-003 and tb-007 are EL-specific.

code_scope.resolution: Gwei-to-Wei scaling is EL-side; Prysm CL handles withdrawal selection only

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does withdrawal processing only increase balances, never decrease?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The balance increase invariant during withdrawal processing is enforced by the Execution Layer's process_withdrawals function. Prysm CL constructs the withdrawal list but does not execute the balance modifications — the EL does. Trust boundary tb-007 is EL-specific.

code_scope.resolution: Balance modification is EL-side; Prysm CL only constructs withdrawal lists
